{noformat}SELECT
    "key", count_of_users, count_of_cash_orders, sum_of_cash_orders, sum_of_debt, debt_sum_ratio, created_date

    created_date = '2023-09-23'
LIMIT 200;{noformat}

{noformat}-33.92:18.420:za
6.4507:3.4710:ng
-1.310:36.817:ke{noformat}

* In relation to the analysis of competition law implications following the increase of the duration of the agreement and the fact that Bolt has reached in PT 50% on average of market share the conclusions are the following:
** The larger market share of Bolt and the longer duration of this new co-invest contract do indeed increase the risk under competition law, in the sense that this sort of agreement may be deemed to lead to foreclosure of the market to Bolt’s competitors.
** Having said this, one has to look at the structure of the market in Portugal, which is made up of two platforms with roughly 50% market share each. Considering the market structure, it is virtually impossible to sustain that any of the operators holds a dominant position. And foreclosure problems under competition law arising from exclusivity and duration are typical manifestations of a dominant position. In the absence of a dominant position and considering the intense competition between both platforms, we consider that a*t this point in time there is a low risk of market foreclosure*.
** However, we recommend that further increases in Bolt’s market share be accompanied by a careful monitoring of exclusivity + duration in agreements, including in co-investment agreements such as the one we are now negotiating.
*  Please note that DLA understands that the current cooperation agreement includes only an upfront discount and eliminates the cash-back bonus mechanism. I propose that we discuss this point on our next call and confirm in particular the following: 
** The upfront discount corresponds to the mechanism that is established in Cl 5.2 of the cooperation agreement whereby Bolt has to pay the Contractor (upfront) the amounts set out in each Request.
** The cashback bonus corresponds to the mechanism that was established in previous Cl 5.6 of the cooperation agreement whereby Bolt had to pay the Contractor 5% of the difference between actual GMV and Target GVM.
*  In any case, DLA considers that both models entail a very low regulatory/banking risk and opting for an upfront discount model will not minimize it significantly.

_10.2. You acknowledge that no employment agreement nor an employment relationship has been or will be established between you and us. # Yes, the Okta authentication currently only works on your local machine. This is a somewhat unfortunate restriction that we hope to resolve in the future, but then again personal accounts are also not really supposed to be used in server environments. If you need a service account for a specific use case, you can request that separately (service accounts don’t require Okta).
# The {{Query has exceeded Scan Raw Bytes Read Limit of 500GB}} limit has nothing to do with the Okta authentication or any SQL client. It is a server-side threshold to prevent individual queries from using too many cluster resources. Most likely it means that you’re scanning a large table without using partition keys, and it’s usually a strong indicator that the query or data layout needs to be optimized.
# You can use the access programmatically. We support any language that can work directly with the JDBC driver (should be any JVM language), and Python via the mentioned JayDeBeApi wrapper. This covers like >95% of all use cases we have. PHP isn’t really widely used within the company, and we don’t have the resources to support it. Nevertheless, you can make it work if you find a wrapper similar to JayDeBeApi for PHP, as mentioned before.
# Opening a new connection prompts the Okta authentication. If this happens for every query, it means that you’re opening a new connection for every query, which isn’t ideal in general.

The *promo code cost/discount* can be +*issued*+ either by Bolt Operations *or* Local Bolt Entities. In order to decide which Bolt Entity (i.e., Bolt Operations or the Local Bolt Entity) should issue the promo code/discount, we should know to which Bolt vertical this promo code/discount refers to and which TP model is applied to that Vertical in the Local Bolt Entity.

We can see which TP model is applied in every market [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2Qiw3tV8_8H9HxbtYlWIUmh2YltohQPRZ5zCo6gT68/edit#gid=1483222946]. At the moment there are 4 markets that are *Local* (Ireland, Poland, Thailand, Tunisia). This means that these 4 markets can only issue promo codes themselves - e.g. CS agent in Lithuania can’t issue a promo code for the rider in Ireland, it must be done by the agent in Ireland. The rest of the markets are *Centralized* and they can issue promo codes to each other, e.g. CS agent in Lithuania can issue a promo code for the rider in Estonia, because all of them are under the Bolt Operations. 

It would be possible to create a process and mention the 4 Local markets, for which promo codes can be only generated locally, but the biggest blocker that I see is that this information can change - right now in [this list|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2Qiw3tV8_8H9HxbtYlWIUmh2YltohQPRZ5zCo6gT68/edit#gid=1483222946] there is a note for Azerbaijan - “CENTRALIZED (Local as of Oct 1)”. There is a risk that we and CS agents won’t be able to always have the latest information about TP models and we can end up having issues with tax/pricing regulations. Also, I’m not sure if we would be able to share that list with OS.

I’ve proposed a shorter version of the code also changing random part {{(PARTITION BY m1.message_id ORDER BY m1.message_id)}} (in case of two or more rows with the same message_id, random one will be picked by {{WHERE rn = 1}} and it will vary between the loads)


{noformat}WITH trim_prop AS (
SELECT
message_id,
message_name,
journey_id,
journey_name,
channel,
delivery_type,
message_type,
LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(CASE WHEN LENGTH(SPLIT(TRIM(message_name), ',')[0]) = 2 THEN TRIM(ARRAY_JOIN(SLICE(SPLIT(message_name, ','), 2,SIZE(SPLIT(message_name, ','))),',')) ELSE message_name END, '[  ,()/.#?!+\&\\-]', '')) AS trimmed_message_name,
CASE 
	WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(lead|registration).*' OR lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(lead|registration).*' THEN 'registration'
 	WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(churn|reactivation).*' OR lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(churn|reactivation).*' THEN 'churn'
	WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(0 times online|new driver|activation).*' OR lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(0 times online|new driver|activation).*' THEN 'activation'
	WHEN lower(message_name) LIKE '%retention%' OR lower(journey_name) LIKE '%retention%' THEN 'retention'
	ELSE NULL
END AS lifecycle_stage1
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_clevertap_driver_campaign_journey_properties
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9
),
keyword AS (
SELECT 
lower(REGEXP_REPLACE(name , '[  ,()/.#?!+\&\\-]', '')) AS keyword_name,
type,
lifecycle_stage 
FROM ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing_spark.driver_lifecycle_comms_label_mapping),
base_chosen_stage as (
select
	trim_prop.message_id,
	trim_prop.message_name,
	trim_prop.journey_id,
	trim_prop.journey_name,
	trim_prop.channel,
	trim_prop.delivery_type,
	trim_prop.message_type,
	trim_prop.trimmed_message_name,
	coalesce(trim_prop.lifecycle_stage1,
	         exact_message_name_match.lifecycle_stage,
	         contain_message_name_match.lifecycle_stage,
	         contain_keyword_name_match.lifecycle_stage,
	         'other/undetermined') as lifecycle_stage
from trim_prop
left join keyword as exact_message_name_match  on
	trimmed_message_name = exact_message_name_match.keyword_name
	and exact_message_name_match.type = 'message_name'
left join keyword as contain_message_name_match  on
	trimmed_message_name like '%' || contain_message_name_match.keyword_name || '%'
	and contain_message_name_match.type = 'message_name'	
left join keyword as contain_keyword_name_match on
	trimmed_message_name like '%' || contain_keyword_name_match.keyword_name || '%'
	and contain_keyword_name_match.type = 'keyword'
	)
,chosen_stage AS (
SELECT
message_id,
lifecycle_stage,
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY message_id ORDER BY lifecycle_stage) AS rn
FROM base_chosen_stage
GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT message_id, lifecycle_stage
  FROM chosen_stage
 WHERE rn = 1{noformat}

Hello, here is the feedback from MT tax authorities:

Bolt Malta Country Manager

Dear Mr Molok,

 Further to our meeting of the 13^th^ September 2023, we are hereby detailing our request for cooperation by Bolt EU as regards the provision of information relating strictly to the economic activity of operators in Malta carrying on their business activities through the Bolt platform.

In this respect, the following information would be specifically relevant for the purpose of ensuring that operators operating in Malta through the Bolt platform are in compliance with the provisions of the VAT Act (Chapter 406, Laws of Malta) and Income Tax Acts (Chapter 123 and 372, Laws of Malta):

# +*Bolt Platform (passenger transport)*+

* VAT registration numbers and Tax Identification Numbers (TIN) of operators operating in Malta utilising the Bolt platform
* In the absence of a VAT registration number, any identification number which identifies the person carrying on an economic activity in Malta
* The total Consideration paid or credited to operators during each calendar quarter during the years 2019 to 2022 split between the operators as identified by their VAT numbers
* Any fees, commissions or taxes withheld or charged by Bolt to the operators in Malta during each calendar quarter during the years 2019 to 2022 split between the operators as identified by their VAT numbers
* The vehicle registration plates used by the operators as identified by their VAT numbers
* Financial Account Identifier in which consideration is paid and Financial institution name, and name of account holder (if available)

+*2. Bolt Food Platform (courier services)*+

* VAT registration numbers and Tax Identification Numbers (TIN) of operators supplying transport services in Malta utilising the Bolt Food platform
* In the absence of a VAT registration number, any identification number which identifies the person carrying on an economic activity in Malta
* The total Consideration paid or credited to operators during each calendar quarter during the years 2019 to 2022 split between the operators as identified by their VAT numbers
* Any fees, commissions or taxes withheld or charged by Bolt to the operators in Malta during each calendar quarter during the years 2019 to 2022 split between the operators as identified by their VAT numbers
* Financial Account Identifier in which consideration is paid and Financial institution name, and name of account holder (if available)

As you may note, this request limits the request to data which is purely data relating to the economic activities of individuals or legal persons and not personal data. The MTCA commits to retaining this data for a period no longer than 3 years and shall be used solely for the purpose of ensuring compliance with the provisions of the VAT Act (Chapter 406, Laws of Malta) and Income Tax Acts (Chapter 123 and 372, Laws of Malta) and for enforcing said provisions. Any information obtained pursuant to such request shall enjoy the obligation of official secrecy by the MTCA as set out in the aforementioned Acts.

We look forward to hearing back from you. Let us know in the meantime if you require anything further from our end.

Yesterday we finally received feedback from our external advisor who was asked to analyse the AT agreement and potential change of payment setup. The conclusions are the following:

* The Partner's right to assign his rights and obligation under Clause 1.7 of OA 2 is valid and enforceable under Estonian law even if it would entitle the Partner to assign the entire agreement to its AT subsidiary.
* Partner is entitled to assign all rights and obligations under OA 2 to its AT subsidiary without any additional consent from Bolt.
* If it comes to such assignment of rights and obligations (in entirety or with respect to some rights and obligations, including the payment obligations towards Bolt) and such assignment will result in the AT subsidiary being required to withhold taxes from payments to Bolt then Clause 5 entitles the AT subsidiary to make such withholdings if this is a legal requirement.

Consequently, we do not have a legal basis to further postpone or push back this change of payment setup.
However, we are entitled to request the Partner to provide us with a copy of the assignment agreement between the Irish entity and the Austrian entity, based on which the Partner assigned its payment obligation to the AT Entity. Please ask Mark Buda to send it to us.

{noformat}WITH trim_prop AS (
SELECT
message_id,
LOWER(
  REGEXP_REPLACE(
    CASE 
    WHEN message_type = 'journey' AND LENGTH(SPLIT(TRIM(journey_name), ',')[0]) = 2 THEN TRIM(ARRAY_JOIN(SLICE(SPLIT(journey_name, ','), 2,SIZE(SPLIT(journey_name, ','))),','))
    WHEN message_type = 'journey' THEN journey_name
    WHEN LENGTH(SPLIT(TRIM(message_name), ',')[0]) = 2 THEN TRIM(ARRAY_JOIN(SLICE(SPLIT(message_name, ','), 2,SIZE(SPLIT(message_name, ','))),',')) ELSE message_name 
    END, '[  ,()/.#?!+\&\\-]', '')) AS trimmed_comms_name,
CASE 
	WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(lead|registration).*' OR lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(lead|registration).*' THEN 'registration'
 	WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(churn|reactivation).*' OR lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(churn|reactivation).*' THEN 'churn'
	WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(0 times online|new driver|activation).*' OR lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(0 times online|new driver|activation).*' THEN 'activation'
	WHEN lower(message_name) LIKE '%retention%' OR lower(journey_name) LIKE '%retention%' THEN 'retention'
	ELSE NULL
END AS lifecycle_stage1
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_clevertap_driver_campaign_journey_properties
GROUP BY 1,2,3
),
keyword AS (
SELECT 
lower(REGEXP_REPLACE(name , '[  ,()/.#?!+\&\\-]', '')) AS keyword_name,
type,
lifecycle_stage 
FROM ng_fivetran_google_sheets_marketing_spark.driver_lifecycle_comms_label_mapping),
base_chosen_stage as (
select
	trim_prop.message_id,
	coalesce(trim_prop.lifecycle_stage1,
	         exact_message_name_match.lifecycle_stage,
	         contain_message_name_match.lifecycle_stage,
	         contain_keyword_name_match.lifecycle_stage,
	         'other/undetermined') as lifecycle_stage
from trim_prop
left join keyword as exact_message_name_match  on
	trimmed_comms_name = exact_message_name_match.keyword_name
	and exact_message_name_match.type = 'message_name'
left join keyword as contain_message_name_match  on
	trimmed_comms_name like '%' || contain_message_name_match.keyword_name || '%'
	and contain_message_name_match.type = 'message_name'	
left join keyword as contain_keyword_name_match on
	trimmed_comms_name like '%' || contain_keyword_name_match.keyword_name || '%'
	and contain_keyword_name_match.type = 'keyword'
	)
,chosen_stage AS (
SELECT
message_id,
lifecycle_stage,
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY message_id ORDER BY lifecycle_stage) AS rn
FROM base_chosen_stage
GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT message_id, lifecycle_stage
  FROM chosen_stage
 WHERE rn = 1 AND message_id IS NOT NULL{noformat}

Hi, 

I can help with the below info:

*For the first question*

According to [+*Ordinance no. 99/2000*+|https://legislatie.just.ro/Public/DetaliiDocument/24110] regarding the marketing of market products and services:

*C. Rules regarding the indication of quantity*

Art. 68. -

(1) Depending on the type and characteristics of the product, on its packaging will be visibly, legibly and unequivocally indicated the dimensions or number of articles (pieces) contained, the net quantity contained, expressed in units of measure recognised by the Romanian state authority in matters of metrology.

(2) The obligation to indicate these data rests with the producer, *packer* or, as the case may be, the importer.

Art. 69. -

*In the case of distance sales (by mail),* any trader who informs the consumer about his product offer by means of catalogues, brochures or other printed publications is obliged to mention, *for pre-packaged products*, the net quantity contained in each package, the selling price, as well as the price per unit of measure, according to the legal provisions in force.

Art. 70. -

(1) *For products sold in bulk (vrac)*, which are weighed or measured _in the presence of the consumer_, the provision of art. 68 para. (1) does not apply.

*(2) The information provided by the measuring devices used to determine the quantity of products sold in bulk (vrac) must be clear and visible to the consumer*.



*For the second question*

For bulk (vrac) products, nutritional and provenance information must be found on the platform. We see a lot of news, retailers get many fines if they don’t specify the country of origin of the fruits and vegetables. 



[+Order no. 420/2008+|https://legislatie.just.ro/Public/DetaliiDocumentAfis/95554] regarding the establishment of the duties of the State Inspection for Technical Control in the Production and Valorisation of Vegetables and Fruits:

* Art. 12 (1) At the retail stage, when the products are packaged, the specific information required by the marketing standards must be legible and visible. 
* (2) For *prepackaged products*, in addition to the information provided by the marketing standards, the net weight is indicated. However, for products normally sold by piece (la bucata) *the requirement to indicate the net weight does not apply if the number of items can be clearly seen and easily counted through the packaging or if the number is indicated on the label*. 
* (3) *The products can be presented by the trader en retail and unpackaged, provided that he displays, alongside the products displayed for sale, a visible and legible notice, which indicates the specific information provided in the marketing standards regarding the variety, the country origin of the product and the quality class to which it belongs*. 
* Art 14 (7) the quality category, the country of origin of the products and, as the case may be, the industrial destination of the product must be indicated on the invoices and documents that accompany the batches of fresh vegetables and fruits. *This requirement is not imposed at the stage of retail sale to the final consumer*.



*Council Regulation (EC)* [+*No 1234/2007*+|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=CONSLEG:2007R1234:20130701:EN:HTML] *of 22 October 2007 establishing a common organisation of agricultural markets and on specific provisions for certain agricultural products*

* Article 113a of Regulation no. 1234/2007, entitled "Additional requirements for the marketing of products from the fruit and vegetable sector", provides in paragraph (1):
* "The products of the fruit and vegetables sector which are intended to be sold fresh to the consumer, may only be marketed if they are sound, fair and of marketable quality and if the country of origin is indicated."



*Implementing Regulation (EU)* [+*no. 543/2011*+|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex%3A32011R0543] *laying down detailed rules for the application of Council Regulation (EC) No 1234/2007 in respect of the fruit and vegetables and processed fruit and vegetables sectors*

* According to Article 3 paragraph (1) of Regulation no. 543/2011, applicable from June 22, 2011, the requirements provided for in article 113a paragraph (1) of Regulation no. 1234/2007 constitutes the general marketing standard which is presented in detail in Part A of Annex I to Implementing Regulation no. 543/2011.
* Part A of Annex I to this implementing regulation provides in point 4, devoted to marking the origin of products, the following:
* "Full name of the country of origin[ (|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex%3A32011R0543#ntr1-L_2011157EN.01005401-E0001][^1^|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex%3A32011R0543#ntr1-L_2011157EN.01005401-E0001][)|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex%3A32011R0543#ntr1-L_2011157EN.01005401-E0001]. For products originating in a Member State this shall be in the language of the country of origin or any other language understandable by the consumers of the country of destination. Art. 26 of Government Emergency Ordinance 49/2019 (ride-hailing law): 

Art. 26. -

*At the request of the authorities with powers in the field, provided by this emergency ordinance, the operator of the digital platform or the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform, as the case may be, will make available to them all the required information that it holds in relation to the performance of the activity by the operators of alternative transport through the digital platform. The provision of this information is carried out in accordance with the legal provisions in force.*

Also, Art. 29. of the same Ordinance provides that:

(1) The control of compliance with the provisions of this emergency ordinance is ensured by:

(…)

*c) National Fiscal Administration Agency*

(…)

(3) At the headquarters of the operator of the digital platform or of the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform in Romania and/or of the alternative transport operator, the control of the alternative transport is carried out by the representatives of the authorities mentioned in para. (1) lit. a) -*c)*, e) and f).



Secondary legislation, _Decision no. 572/2020_ also mentions at Art. 11:

*the representation mandate of the subsidiary ratified by the operator of the digital platform, in which all the rights and obligations conferred on it are mentioned; the right/obligation to make available to public institutions, in accordance with their competences, the data relating to journey, route, passengers, drivers, transport operators, car, location, contracts must be expressly specified;*

Possible Special cat data issues regarding the disclosure of this information - While the data on Riders would initially be anonymous, we would have to refuse to provide any Rider data in connection with these cancellations since, with the Rider data, we would be inadvertently disclosing special cat data. We would have to consider any future Rider data disclosure in connection with the data we are providing regarding cancellations.

Applying a ‘motivated intruder’ test, we would also need to consider that the Council would potentially have access to hosing records, electoral registers and benefits registers which could provide the Council with the identity of the Rider (if we consider the pick-up or drop-off address could be the home address of the Rider).

I would anticipate not sharing Rider contact information would be a major sticking point in the future since the Council would not be able to investigate these issues.

The special category issues are created by Bolt since the rides which we would consider as unjustified cancellations are focussed around traits which would trigger special cat data considerations (use of wheelchair, gender, religion are all basses which Bolt consider unjustified cancellation reasons).

My opinion is that we would need to be extremely hesitant to provide this cancellation data under its current design due to the special category data risk.

_Venturing into B2G exposes Bolt to a reclassification risk in the sense that the relationship between Bolt and the drivers on the Bolt platform could be reclassified as an employment, if tried in court. A reclassification results in several negative consequences and obligations for Bolt. The specific consequenses will not be covered in this document as it requires an in-depth legal analysis which will be conducted at a later stage. The assumption is that a reclassification scenario should be avoided._ 

_Tender requirements within B2G demand certain control mechanisms to be put in place between Bolt and the drivers and additional controls would be required to avoid fines for failed trips. Control imposed by Bolt on drivers (see examples below) is the key element in a reclassification assessment and Bolt would have to make an overall assessment of the specific control mechanisms in order to assess how high the reclassification risk indeed would be within B2G and how this may affect Bolt’s existing ride-hailing vertical (reclassification may have a spill-over effect)._ 

_Examples of factors that increase the reclassification risk:_

* _All drivers who are allowed to drive children without supervision, are required to undergo background checks (in addition to the one performed by the transport authority);_ 
* _Drivers are required to wear uniforms;_ 
* _Extensive requirements to train drivers in multiple fields;_ 
* _Scheduling of cars/fleets/drivers will probably be required;_ 
* _Bolt will likely be required to act as principal instead of agency due to tender requirements._

Hey [~accountid:61d2d14649f19500692630cd]!

As agreed during our little chat regarding e.g. dish washing machines in the office last week, I have looked into whether there are any 'Swedish standards' when it comes to division of the responsibility for different types of maintenance at the office between the landlord and the tenant in commercial lease agreements. 

*Legal framework:*

As a main rule under Swedish law, the landlord shall do the required maintenance to keep the lease object in usable condition, which may, in some cases, include the responsibility of switching out old dish washing machines at own cost. The starting point in the law is namely that the *landlord is responsible for principally all maintenance* - but only *unless otherwise agreed*. It is common to agree that the tenant must be responsible for internal maintenance of the premises, i.e. surface layer of floors, walls and ceiling while the landlord must carry out other maintenance of the premises and of the furnishings provided by the landlord. 

In light of the above, my assessment is that having to replace the dish washing machines ourselves is not necessarily the standard, or at least it’s not obvious that we should be responsible for this. In other words, what responsibility we will have for maintenance in the coming years will completely depend on what the agreement says. 

*This leads us to the agreement:*

I have taken a closer look at the current agreement. Currently, the landlord’s maintenance responsibilities mentioned above are in principle completely transferred to us under the agreement. We could try to negotiate this, either with the aim to limit our responsibility for maintenance and repairs on a general level, or, based on what you told me regarding the recurring need for dishwasher maintenance in this office, alternatively with the aim of limiting Bolt’s liability in relation to _specific items_. 

As an example, the latter could be a clause stating something like “as regards dishwasher X, our liability for repairs and maintenance is limited to [a specific number of repairs/amount spent on repairs] per year”, and that any liability exceeding that limitation must be carried by the landlord. The latter type of clause may be an effective way of mitigating risks associated with the deterioration of specific items, like the expensive repairs of dishwashers, but otherwise it would be maintaining status quo. [~accountid:63ee3904601ad5efa51309ee] I would very much appreciate your input on this from a real estate perspective, e.g. would such clauses be uncommon in your experience?

*Next steps*

With the above background, if you still want to negotiate the agreement in respect of items other than the index clause and term as mentioned earlier, I think the easiest way to do this would be asking for the draft addendum from the representative. 

Lastly, I remember you told me that the landlord often referred to a specific clause in the current agreement when you brought up maintenance requests in the past. Do you remember exactly which clause/clauses they referred to? 

Thank you 🙏

Best,

Ida

I am not an expert, but 8 km is not enough of a distance to cause such damage to the sidewall. Speaking from personal experience, the damage looks like done over a longer period - more like several hundred kilometers.

We have had several cases where someone finds a damage that noone has reported before and we aren’t able to pinpoint the moment the damage was done.

Currently, speaking strictly from legal pov, we are not able to rule out the fact that this damage might have occured while the person finished the ride and the the new customer started theirs.

Hey!

Let’s take very likely scenario - the pressure in the tyre is 1,2 bar; not low enough to be visually seen if not inspected closely and not high enough to protect the rim from the impact. NB! drop from 2,2 → 1,2 might trigger the speed sensor warning, but it definitely should trigger pressure sensor warning.

Let’s say the previous user, or the one before that pushed the “SET” button in the vehicle and the user didn’t see the error message on the dashboard - in that case, the unlucky last user get the cumulative blame (and damage) for all the users, even if they are not directly (or fully) responsible.

I am saying, this is not a clear cut case and if we don’t have any evidence supporting our case (photos? logs? inspection?) we’d be better off either reaching a compromise or dropping the case.

NB! If the logs show that they were speeding, then we could use it to our advantage.

*ELI5 summary of the agreement:*

* Bolt wants to make some changes to the laws about rides in Latvia, and KPMG will help them with that.
* KPMG and Bolt have already worked together to make a report about how ride platforms affect the economy, and now they want to continue working on changing the laws. They will have workshops where they talk to important people from the government about what needs to be changed.
* KPMG will help organize these workshops and make sure they go well. They will also do some research to make a plan for the changes they want to make. In the end, KPMG will give Bolt a document with their plan for the new laws.
* The document will explain what changes they want to make and why they think the changes are important. KPMG will start working on this as soon as the contract is signed and they get paid.
* They will finish their work within *12 weeks* and give Bolt the final document *one week after they get feedback on the draft.* Bolt will have to pay KPMG for their work, and they will also *have to pay for any expenses that KPMG has while doing the work*.
* If there are any changes or extra work that comes up, Bolt will have to pay for that too. Both parties have to agree to the terms of the contract and sign it for it to be valid.

*The scope:*

* The first thing KPMG will do is organize three workshops.
* In the first workshop, they will talk about the main problems in the rides market and what has been done before to solve them. 
* In the second workshop, everyone will share their opinions and try to agree on what changes should be made to the laws about rides. 
* In the third workshop, they will look at a first draft of the changes and make sure it includes everyone's ideas. 
* KPMG will take care of all the details for these workshops, like finding a place to have them, inviting the right people, and making notes about what is talked about.
* After the workshops, KPMG will use what they learned to create a document called a draft legislative proposal. This document will have ideas for changing the laws about rides, based on what was discussed in the workshops. KPMG will do some research to make sure the ideas are good and will work well. They will look at what other industries and countries have done in similar situations. In doing all of this, KPMG will use the information that Bolt and its employees give them.
* They will trust that the information is true and won't check if it is true or not.

*The result:*

* KPMG will be preparing a document for the Client called a draft legislative proposal. This document will have information about changes that need to be made to a law in Latvia that is about road transportation.
* The draft legislative proposal will include a few different things. First, there will be a summary of each change that needs to be made in the law. Then, there will be the suggested new wording for each part of the law that needs to be changed. And finally, there will be a short explanation of why each change is needed. This explanation can include things like talking to different people, looking at how other industries work, or studying what other countries do.
* The quality of the changes that KPMG can make in the law will depend on the information that the Client gives them. If the Client doesn't give KPMG all the important information or gives them the wrong information, KPMG can't be held responsible if the changes in the law aren't good.

Hi [~accountid:5f7aaad6021acf0076d55a90] , in my understanding the justifiable character of the request is linked with the information in the request and the power of the authority to request certain data.

Following article 5 of Lei n.º 68/2019, de 27 de Agosto (Estatuto do Ministério Público), available in the following link [https://www.pgdlisboa.pt/leis/lei_mostra_articulado.php?nid=3119&tabela=leis&so_miolo=|https://www.pgdlisboa.pt/leis/lei_mostra_articulado.php?nid=3119&tabela=leis&so_miolo=|smart-link] , “_All public and private entities have the duty to collaborate with the Public Prosecutor's Office, providing documents and information and clarifications_ *_requested in a duly justified manner according to the competence to be exercised, within the limits of the law,_* _without prejudice to the applicable secrecy regimes”_

Hence, when reviewing the request we need to confirm:

*a) is the request justified?* Yes, the authority provides the reasons for the request

*b) is the request within the competences of the authority?*

Here I would verify in particular the autority in relation to the following data: IP, date/time from where the trips requested are associated; from which device the requests where made and mobile phone number (including if different from previous trips).

According to article 14 of the cyber crime law, _4 - The provisions of this article shall apply to_ *_service providers_* _who may be_ *_ordered to communicate_* _to the procedure data_ *_relating to their customers or subscribers, including any information other than traffic or content data, contained in the form of computer data or in any other form_*_, held by the service provider, which makes it possible to determine:_
_a) The type of communication service used, the technical measures taken in this regard and the period of service;_
_(b) the identity, postal or geographical address and telephone number of the subscriber, and any other access number, billing and payment data available on the basis of a contract or service agreement; or_
_(c) any other information on the location of the communication equipment, available on the basis of a contract or service agreement._

Hence, it appears that the information being requested can be order to providers such as Bolt and only the Public Prosecutor would have such powers according to the Second Instance Lisbon Court determined in[ |http://www.dgsi.pt/jtrl.nsf/33182fc732316039802565fa00497eec/eb1460fa14510bf380257d080036a9b9?OpenDocument][+Ac. TRL de 19-06-2014+|http://www.dgsi.pt/jtrl.nsf/33182fc732316039802565fa00497eec/eb1460fa14510bf380257d080036a9b9?OpenDocument]+.+

Dear all, 

 

According to the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) personal data controller determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data. Processor engages in personal data processing only on the behalf of the controller.

 

Bolt determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data: customers submit their personal data to Bolt as food delivery platform coordinator. Bolt collects and processes customers` personal data because it is necessary for coordination: performance of a food purchase/delivery contract to which the customer is party. This means that *Bolt is personal data controller.* 





Reitan Convenience Latvia (Reitan) does not need customers` personal data and engages in personal data processing only on the behalf of the Bolt (controller). This is a reason why *Reitan is not independent controller.* 

 

According to the Specific conditions for Schedule 2 of the Agreement for use of Bolt Food platform concluded/signed between Bolt and Reitan *Bolt is controller of personal data and Reitan is processor, and not* i*ndependent controllers* as you define it.

Hi @Carlos Casio Pérez ! Of course. This is a tricky request so I will give you a little bit of context on the tax issue and try to make the issue and the request clear.

Romania intends to implement an e-invoicing system as of 1 January 2024. In an initial phase, this would only apply to transactions between business entities and Romanian companies. The process of adapting our systems to it is complicated and will take time. Not complying with the e-invoicing rules is subject to a penalty of up to € 805 per invoice. In this context, I already asked for information regarding the number of invoices issued by the Romanian company to business customers in 2023 and make an estimate of the contingency for 2024 in case we are not able to issue those invoices.

Last week the Romanian Government published the draft of the law that includes e-invoicing and it seems that the e-invoicing obligation will also apply to non-resident companies that are registered for VAT purposes in Romania (which is the case of Bolt Operations OU - VAT number: RO42717800). Accordingly, any invoices issued by Bolt Operations OU using its Romanian VAT number to Romanian business customers will need to comply with the e-invoice rules. In order to make an estimate of the amount of the contingency, I need to know the number of invoices issued by Bolt Operations OU during a given timeframe (e.g. 2023) with these conditions (using Romanian VAT number + to business customers). I am assuming that this can only happen in ride hailing (commission invoices issued to fleets / drivers), and bolt food (also commission invoices). Bolt Market is localised and I assume Bolt Rentals does not have business customers. This is the reason for the first request: _1 - A report with the list of invoices issued by Bolt Ops directly to Romanian business customers (with column regarding price and VAT) - please consider only invoices issued by Bolt Ops using its Romanian VAT number;_

In addition to the problem referred to above, there is a second contingency that might be at stake and is the following: within the food business, Bolt Operations OU issues invoices on behalf of Romanian entities (couriers) to clients that nay be business. The invoicing flow is the following:

Accordingly, as of 1 January 2024 these entities (for which we issue invoices on behalf) may also have comply with the e-invoicing rules in case of business clients. If the invoices issued by these entities have to be e-invoices, then Bolt Operations OU, by being the entity issuing invoices on behalf, should also comply with the rules. Thank you and feel free to ask any questions on the above.

Hello again [~accountid:616ff0d6702bd0006a685f65] ,

I have now taken a closer look at this ticket. Thank you for the detailed background.

*In summary,* my assessment is that from a legal perspective, there are no obstacles preventing you from paying out the balance (regardless of whether it exceeds 50 SEK or not) under Swedish law. If Swedish law applies, the relevant partners may claim payment of unpaid balance for 10 years following the delivery to which the relevant payment claim refers. 

Whether or not we have an _obligation_ to pay out unpaid balance would be regulated by the T&Cs (which I have not been able to locate, will check with my team if you don’t know either - see below), at least in the cases where partners have failed to provide correct bank details etc. 

Please see further details below 👇 

*The statutory limitation in Sweden is generally 10 years* (but the period can be extended). This means that, if Swedish law applies, partners have a right to claim payment of any unreceived earnings for 10 years following the date when Bolt’s payment obligation arose, i.e. the date when the partner provided the relevant service to which the payment claim relates. However, whether or not you should keep the payout route during this time period is not a legal issue, but rather a business decision that may need to be taken in collaboration with accounting. 

*In any event, I am unsure whether Swedish law applies to your question*, as the relevant law, the Swedish Act on Limitation (1981:130) (_Swe: Preskriptionslagen_), only applies where Swedish law is the applicable substantive law governing the contractual obligation on which the payment claim is based. 

I’m not mistaken, the T&Cs for partners that applied in the Swedish delivery vertical, based on which any claims for unreceived earnings by partners would be made, were governed by Estonian law. In that case, the Swedish statutory limitation period for civil claims is not applicable to the unpaid balance that this ticket concerns.

* *Question:* I cannot seem to locate the T&Cs which used to apply for delivery in Sweden. Do you by chance know whether the T&Cs stated that they were governed by Estonian law? If not, just let me know and I will check with my team.

Also, please note that there may be privacy aspects to how long we can keep storing any personal data relating to our (ex-)partners of the closed down Delivery vertical. If not done already, this should be checked with the privacy team to ensure that we are compliant with our legal obligations relating to storing of personal data. 

Please get back to me on the above and let me know if you have any additional questions or comments. 

Best regards,

Ida

[~accountid:637dde50fde064eda2edd049]  from what I understood in our conversation is that journey_name should take precedence over message name. 
Please note, that we would need some changes to the query to implement this. Please note following query:


{noformat}with test_data as 
(
select 'registration' as message_name, 'registration' as journey_name 
union ALL
select 'churn' as message_name, 'registration' as journey_name
union ALL
select 'registration' as message_name, 'churn' as journey_name
UNION ALL 
select 'no_match' as message_name, 'retention' as journey_name
UNION ALL 
select 'retention' as message_name, 'no_match' as journey_name
UNION ALL 
select 'no_match' as message_name, 'no_match' as journey_name
)
SELECT
	message_name
	, journey_name
, CASE 
	WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(lead|registration).*' OR lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(lead|registration).*' THEN 'registration'
	WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(churn|reactivation).*' OR lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(churn|reactivation).*' THEN 'churn'
	WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(0 times online|new driver|activation).*' OR lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(0 times online|new driver|activation).*' THEN 'activation'
	WHEN lower(message_name) LIKE '%retention%' OR lower(journey_name) LIKE '%retention%' THEN 'retention' END as lifecycle
from test_data{noformat}


Which returns:

!image-20230927-120125.png|width=433,height=186!



This shows, that it’s rather registration > churn > activation > retention gradation, rather than journey > message.

For journey > message precedence we would need code like that:


{noformat}with test_data as 
(
select 'registration' as message_name, 'registration' as journey_name 
union ALL
select 'churn' as message_name, 'registration' as journey_name
union ALL
select 'registration' as message_name, 'churn' as journey_name
UNION ALL 
select 'no_match' as message_name, 'retention' as journey_name
UNION ALL 
select 'retention' as message_name, 'no_match' as journey_name
UNION ALL 
select 'no_match' as message_name, 'no_match' as journey_name
)
SELECT
  message_name
  , journey_name
, CASE 
  WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(lead|registration).*' THEN 'registration'
  WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(churn|reactivation).*' THEN 'churn'
  WHEN lower(message_name) REGEXP '.*(0 times online|new driver|activation).*' THEN 'activation'
  WHEN lower(message_name) LIKE '%retention%' THEN 'retention' END as message_lifecycle
, CASE 
  WHEN lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(lead|registration).*' THEN 'registration'
  WHEN lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(churn|reactivation).*' THEN 'churn'
  WHEN lower(journey_name) REGEXP '.*(0 times online|new driver|activation).*' THEN 'activation'
  WHEN lower(journey_name) LIKE '%retention%' THEN 'retention' END as journey_lifecycle
,COALESCE(journey_lifecycle, message_lifecycle) AS lifecycle -- here precedence of journey over message take place
from test_data{noformat}

Hey Aisma,

Having topups (in other words automatic charges) have nothing to do with the Billing strategy 🙂 It is related to payment strategy.

# {{Credit Card}}, in which monthly invoices are automatically charged for *every ride*; or
# {{Post-paid}}, in which client
## needs to transfer the amounts manually, or
## can add a credit card to charge it once a month.

Both of these payment strategies are applicable to both billing strategies (intermediary and resale). In other words, you can see topups in each billing strategy. 

If you see a topup after each ride, that means the company is “Credit card” payment strategy. If the topup is once a month, that means the company is “Post-paid” but added a credit card to their profile (completely optional). 

To give you the most relevant info: this company is an intermediary company with postpaid payment strategy.

Please let me know if you have further questions 🙂

That’s correct, you requested 42,5 days so far. But we also have to keep in mind carryover rules that are set in South Africa. If you are left with unused vacation days by the end of your period, it’s being carried over to the next year, but they are on your balance only for 6 months - if they are not used within 6 months - they are forfeited. 

So what happened so far:

*01/03/2021 till 31/02/2022*: you accrued 20 days - 7,5 days of vacation = 12,54 days of vacation left (they carried over to the next period) → 

*01/03/2022 till 31/02/2023*: you accrued 20 days + 12,54 days (carryover from previous period) - 3,54 days of carryover forfeited (you didn’t use your carryover in full that period) = 29 days. During this period you requested 20 days of vacation in total = 9 days of vacation left (they carried over to the next period) → 

*01/03/2023 till 31/02/2024*: 20 days accrued + 9 days of carryover = 29 days. During this period you already have 15 days of vacation requested (29 - 15) = 14 days of vacation left.

I would like to revisit the topic because I believe we may be overlooking an important detail. The reason for including specific information in the document quality block is to clarify that it is not related to the document's quality. The block is actually implemented for various reasons and only the compliance team can provide accurate information to the driver- they can’t provide it to CS. An audit revealed that this was often the case.

-> they are further lower, most in the {{170-220 ms}} range
* when we fetch more than 1000 items from {{elasticsearch}} the calls are made in parallel, one call per slice (one slice = 1000 items), so for >11k items 12 calls are made in parallel to {{elasticsearch}} to fetch each slice
* the methodology here seems correct, although a call for 3 slices takes {{50-60 ms}} as observed, so even this does not scale somehow; but given the full context this does not look like "the bottleneck"

Some conclusions:

* {{/getMenuCategories}} does stuff after it fetches the actual menu items, like building a menu graph and enriching the items with extra data which does not seem to scale gracefully, will investigate if improvements can be made here
* the way we call {{elasticsearch}} seems correct, although the parallelism does not scale as well; improving this however won't dramatically affect the response time of the public endpoint so I would focus on the first point above
* I attach a video to compare how Uber Eats responds vs Bolt Food when dealing with large menus and it looks very similar to me, just to put things into perspective

Hi, [~accountid:5fbb6251d670b8006ea1ad00]! Thank you for reaching out and sorry for the delay in getting back to you. We have reviewed the NDA and the comments of the Partner in relation to our General Terms, please see our opinion below.

*General Terms*

We can see that the version of the General Terms that the client reviewed is not an up-to-date one. It is the June 2022 version and on the website we have the [+*December 2022 version*+|https://static.food.bolt.eu/legalDocument/2DKHjniYcVpGXB0QQnaV2a/V5%20of%20Bolt-Partner%20General%20Terms%20(RO)%20-ENG-RO-.pdf].

# Partner replaced original clause 5.5 and added a new wording: “_Bolt is responsible for and undertakes to ensure the uninterrupted operation of the Bolt Food Platform and will also provide technical support for the effective operation of the Bolt Food Platform on any device (including any operating system). Partners undertake to install and/or use all updates, upgrades or modules provided by Bolt. Bolt shall not be liable for any damage or loss of profit caused by Partner's failure to comply with the obligation set forth in this Section 5.5._”.
*Answer:* We cannot entirely agree with the proposed changes because we cannot provide uninterrupted operation. Please try to explain to the Partner that it is unusual to guarantee uninterrupted provision of any software, because software requires maintenance and there could be interruptions caused by other underlying services. This is the wording that we can suggest:
“_Bolt is responsible for and undertakes to ensure the_ -_uninterrupted_- _operation of the Bolt Food Platform and will also provide_ *_reasonable_* _technical support for the effective operation of the Bolt Food Platform_ -_on any device (including any operating system)_-_. Partners undertake to install and/or use all updates, upgrades or modules provided by Bolt. Bolt shall not be liable for any damage or loss of profit caused by Partner's failure to comply with the obligation set forth in this Section 5.5._”
# Partner amended clause 8.2: “If either Party breaches its obligations under this Agreement, any applicable laws or regulations retained by a final court judgment, disparages the other Party or damages the other Party's brand, reputation or business, as such disparagement and/or damages are retained by a final court judgment, or if Bolt reasonably suspects fraudulent actions committed by the Partner while using the Bolt Food Platform, the aggrieved Party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement without notice and without any obligation to compensate for lost profits.”.
*Answer:* We cannot agree to the proposed amendments.The right to terminate the Agreement without notice is granted to the Partner by clause 8.4, so there is no great benefit in making this clause mutual. Also, clause 8.2 allows Bolt to suspend the Partner on the Platform and proceed with extraordinary termination and the new wording removes the right to suspend the Partner. We require the protection from claims regarding loss of profits in case the reason for termination was some kind of serious violation, including non-compliance with the applicable law, by the Partner. Perhaps Partner will agree if you can provide them with our reasons which I set out here. 
# Partner requested deletion of clause 8.3.3: “can demonstrate that the Partner concerned has repeatedly infringed these General Terms, resulting in the termination of the provision of the whole of the online intermediation services in question.”
*Answer:* We cannot agree to this suggestion because some infringements might be quite serious and will require quicker reaction, so it might not be reasonable to wait 30 days to terminate the agreement.
# Partner requested deletion of clause 12.10: “The Partner shall indemnify and hold Bolt harmless from and against any and all claims and liabilities, costs, and expenses (including the reasonable fees of attorneys and other professionals) which result from or arise out of (i) the use of the Partner’s name, trade mark or any other materials (including the photos of Goods) by Bolt in accordance with Section 9; or (ii) breach by the Partner of any representation, warranty, covenant or obligation contained in this Agreement.”
*Answer:* We cannot agree to this suggestion as we require this protection. This clause is not about liability per se, but it is all about holding Bolt harmless in case there are claims by third parties due to some kind of Partner’s fault. These type of clauses are standard in these kinds of agreements.
# Partner raised some questions regarding Section 14: “On what legal basis is this ranking made and what are the legal, concrete criteria considered? Is the European legislation on fair competition respected?”.
*Answer:* Bolt complies with competition rules and in case the Partner spotted any specific issues then we would be glad to know and discuss. They can find information about rankings in clause 5.3 and section 14. Can you please ask them to describe their specific concern?
# Partner is concerned about a mistake in clause 14.1 that makes reference to clause 5.32.
*Answer:* The correct reference is 5.3 as per English version of the T&Cs.
# Partner made several amendments to Schedule 2 - Data Processing Agreement.
*Answer:* We shall provide them with a [*newer version of our T&Cs*|https://static.food.bolt.eu/legalDocument/2DKHjniYcVpGXB0QQnaV2a/V5%20of%20Bolt-Partner%20General%20Terms%20(RO)%20-ENG-RO-.pdf] where we have a data sharing agreement and some of their issues will be addressed there.

Please let me know if I missed or there are any other points raised by the Partner.

Also, please make sure that you prepare special terms for this Partner by using the template for Romania available on this [+*page*+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2577203498/Bolt+Food+Terms+Conditions+and+Templates]. It seems that the Partner assumes that they need to amend our General Terms directly, but this is not the case - all changes shall be specified in the special terms.

To speed up the review process next time please review the comments of the Partner and outline clearly in English any concerns that the Partner may have.



*NDA*

Is there a possibility that they will agree to use our [+*template*+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/11bbb_-X7f_6eOiNdz-P5qThfHhZIxF2ItzhV4szQKUg/edit?usp=sharing] of the NDA? Their NDA is quite controversial and ambiguous because it seems that they did some kind of machine translation.

Hi [~accountid:641d70192cee496759ec78f0] the process with response to authorities is [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/4040950288/Requests+from+Authorities+or+Police|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/4040950288/Requests+from+Authorities+or+Police|smart-link] and it is the duty of CS to respond to these requests. For the rest of the requests, you have to rely on the law, data principles and what is pragmatic-there are no policies for all these forms. Also check with privacy team-they are best placed to give guidance.

Hey [~accountid:62d01789bd54f8d3ffb6c03d] and [~accountid:61dd8fc3f63ac80070cdf28a],

Please find an update below.

*Is it possible to appeal the moving of the vehicles?*

No. Under lag om flyttning av fordon i vissa fall (_Eng (unofficial) translation: Swedish law on moving vehicles in certain cases_), 10 §, It is not possible to appeal the decision of moving the vehicle. 

*If appeal is not possible, what can we do instead?*

Instead, Bolt must contest the payment claim for the impound charges from the authority who impounded the vehicle, e.g. Stockholm stad.

*How can we contest the payment claim for the impound charges?*

To contest the payment claim for the impound charges from the authority who impounded the vehicle, e.g. Stockholm stad, Bolt should contact Stockholm stad with the claim informing them that it believes that the claim is incorrect. At this point, Stockholm stad might ask Bolt for any information that could substantiate Bolt's claim, such as a police report if the vehicle was taken from you through an act of crime or any evidence, such as pictures, making it likely that the parking was lawful in the first place, depending on the basis for the impoundment. If Stockholm stad does not accept this and continues to assert the claim the matter will proceed in court.

*Do we (Nordics legal) recommend proceeding with the matter in court?*

Although it is possible to proceed with the matter in court as above, we do not recommend it. This is mainly for the following reasons:

* As a rule, we do not have the sufficient material to substantiate our claim as required to win the case (see above)
* Proceedings in court would require substantial resource, both internal and external, to the point where it likely is not possible to motivate given that the chances of winning the case are low (see next bullet point below)
* [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7] and I have discussed our legal position from a general point of view with respect to this issue, and our summary assessment is that the court would most likely not rule in our favour. The impoundment would need to be deemed wrongful from a legal perspective by the court, and even though impounding e-vehicles that are parked only centimetres outside the designated parking square is inappropriate, it is not exactly wrong from a legal perspective.

*What do we (Nordics legal) recommend?*

* We recommend handing this over to public policy to start communication and building on a strong relationship with Stockholm stad and any other necessary municipality/city. 
* Public policy can hopefully start affecting how the municipalities/cities make their assessments of parked e-vehicles. 
* Also, public policy could lobby for law amendment or guidelines for interpretation purposes that should apply to the municipalities/cities' assessments. 

Please let me know if you have any questions or if you need anything further.

Best regards,

Ida

Query for testing:

{noformat}%sql
SELECT
    o.delivery_lat,
    substr(o.delivery_lat,1,6) substr_lat,
    round(o.delivery_lat ,3) round_lat,
    substr(o.delivery_lat,1,6)|| ':' || substr(o.delivery_lng,1,6) || ':' || co.country_code AS key,
    round(o.delivery_lat ,3)|| ':' || round(o.delivery_lng ,3) || ':' || co.country_code AS key_round,
    co.user_id AS user_id,
    co.order_id AS order_id,
    co.user_price_eur AS price_eur,
    CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem OR co.is_chargeback OR co.is_final_failed_payment THEN co.order_id ELSE NULL END AS fraud_payment
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co   
LEFT JOIN ng_delivery_spark.delivery_order_order o ON co.order_id = o.id AND co.city_id = o.city_id
WHERE co.created_date >= DATE(DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, -3))
    AND co.order_type = 'food_delivery'
    AND co.order_state = 'finished'
    AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
    AND o.delivery_lat in (34.699814,-1.265123,-33.922538,-34.047607,44.419804,44.435573){noformat}

Hi [~accountid:60528926695c3900706cc798] 

According to Bolt Legal Contracting Standards the contract should not be more than 1 year, however, the importance of the term becomes less relevant if Bolt has a strong termination for convenience right. Bolt should have the right to terminate the contract for convenience, ideally by notifying the other party not more than 30-90 days in advance. If having a right to terminate for convenience becomes an issue in negotiations, the reasonable middle ground may be to include a minimum initial term, before which a party cannot exercise the right to terminate for convenience. Also in most cases, the contract should not automatically renew, especially if the contract provides for recurring fees. 

Currently we have contract for 3 years + auto renewal for 3 years. We can terminate it early only till 1st April 2024 so we don’t have strong termination for convenience right. 

Based on this I would propose:

* reduce contract period and 
* prolong early termination clause period or
* include termination for convenience right for Bolt with 30-90 day notice period

This could be relevant if we would want to engage with other similar training providers for better price or in other situations when we would like to terminate this contract.

Hey [~accountid:641d70192cee496759ec78f0]!

*Provision of general information regarding financials to the trustee*

Like [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7] indicated below, we usually cooperate with liquidators/trustees in the Nordics when it comes to providing information about financials, i.e. unpaid balance to the driver/fleet for transportation services already provided and  information about to what account we have sent payments in the past. The same applies for Norway. The relevant rules are set out in the Norwegian Bankruptcy Act ‘_Lov om gjeldsforhandling og konkurs (konkursloven)’ (_as referred to in the ruling that you kindly translated above).

*Provision of sign in-details or driver/fleet’s user account to the trustee*

Regarding the the question of whether we can give the liquidator an account to sign in to the bankrupt fleet’s driver account, my assessment is that this is rather a contractual question than a question regulated by the Bankruptcy Act. Please see some information that I have been able to collect about this in the bullet points below.

* It depends on whether the liquidator has a right to enter into the contract between the fleet and Bolt under Norwegian mandatory bankruptcy law (our assessment is that setting up an account specifically for the bankruptcy estate to sign in to the driver account would be accepting that the bankruptcy estate enters into the bankrupt fleet’s contract with Bolt). 
* The question of whether such mandatory right exists for the bankruptcy estate is regulated by the Norwegian law _‘Lov om fordringshavernes dekningsrett (dekningsloven)’_. 
* There are some exceptions when the bankruptcy estate does not have such a mandatory right, one of them being when the nature of the contract would prevent the bankruptcy estate from taking the bankrupt debtor’s place in the context of the contract. I believe this exception should apply in this particular situation, as the nature of all contracts between drivers/fleets and Bolt entails a requirement for the driver or fleet to have the necessary (taxi-) license as is required under Norwegian law to provide the relevant transportation services. 
* In summary, my assessment is that we do not have to provide the liquidator with sign in details as the liquidator/bankruptcy estate is unable to perform the contractual obligations of the bankrupt fleet under the contract with Bolt (and would also not be qualified in the first place since the license is a requirement on our end to create a Bolt driver account) and, therefore, does not have any mandatory right under Norwegian law to take over the bankrupt fleet’s contract with Bolt. 

I hope this helps. Please feel free to reach out if you have any further questions on the above or anytime you need help with other Nordics-related legal issues. 🙂 

Best,

Ida

*Employers have the obligation to pay taxes and social security contributions (contributions to the insurance schemes implemented by the government).* Sums such as taxes and social security contributions are deducted from gross salaries and paid to some governmental organisms before net salary is paid to the employee. 

In public procurement procedures - which should be harmonised at EU level- *authorities need to make sure that selected operators are running their businesses in compliance with the law, including social, labor and tax law.* 

To this extent, in the framework of the tender for rentals in Bruxelles, we are asked to *produce a formal declaration in front of a notary*  +*unless*+ *there’s EE public registry/ authority that can issue this type of documents*. 

For example:

* In Belgium for instance ONSS can issue a document stating that the company has fulfilled its tax and social security obligations. 
* In FR that would be URSSAF.

Hi [~accountid:712020:8c797c70-7a57-496e-aa3f-5d91df806eb2] ! I have. 

The main tax aspects to consider are: 

# The agency fee should be subject to withholding tax at a 2% rate under the double tax treaty between Estonia and Romania. For this purpose, Bolt Ops will have to deliver a tax residency certificate to Auchan Romania. Otherwise a 16% rate applies.
# The invoices issued by Bolt Ops need to include a reference to the reverse charge mechanism.

Both tax aspects are in line with what is being done in the Bolt Food platform in Romania. No issues here.

I do note that clause 8 states that in exchange for using the Bolt Food Platform +_and the Bolt Market Trademark_+ the Partner undertakes to pay Bolt the Agency Fee. I understand the payment for the use of the Bolt Market Trademark should not be considered a commission (agency fee) for tax purposes but rather a royalty. I think that within a tax audit the tax authorities could sustain this argument. This would lead to the issue of quantifying the amount of the components that should be allocated to the use of the platform and the use of the trademark, and a 10% withholding tax rate would be applied on the latter (instead of 2%). 

The liability for the obligation to withhold tax is on Auchan and therefore this point may be raised by their counsel. However, although the liability is Auchan’s, if Bolt Ops is collecting the cash and deducting the agency fee before performing the payout to Auchan, Bolt Ops has to consider the - correct - withholding tax in order to avoid having Auchan claiming we did not provide them with the correct amount of tax to be delivered to the Romanian tax authorities.

-> Brussels has also learnt and not longer explicitly wants a Belgian document, foreign equivalent. if that document doesn’t exist (as is the case in EE), Bot OPs OU can make a a solemn declaration before a judicial or administrative authority, a notary or a qualified professional body in that country to declare itself that it doesn’t have social debts.

_“Hey! I just spoke to Comet, the translation service (who turned out to be more of a legalisation + any additional services platform, including translation). The man I spoke to, Christopher, was very helpful. He explained that Qatar and other Arabic countries are usually pretty straight forward and easy when it comes to commercial PoAs. He said that it is not common to translate the document to Arabic (ie a dual language version) but instead English principally always works fine. He could help with all of the services, sending to the notary, Swedish ministry and then Qatar Embassy, or we can do it ourselves. What he also told me that was good information to have is that the Qatar Embassy in Stockholm is one of the few embassies that take the longest time when it comes to legalisation services. They take about 1 week to give a price once the document has been submitted, then 1 more week for the legalisation to be completed, so two weeks in total. He said that can sometimes be pushed if we explain that the matter is urgent; "just give us a price and we will pay right away" and then at least the "giving a price"-part of the process takes a few days less. I have now received the advice from our external lawyer on the letter Bolt received from Trowers & Hamlin on 12 September 2023. 

This letter is a Rent Authority Letter. This letter is informing Bolt of the change in ownership in the property,  and advising Bolt that future payments due under the lease should be made to the new owner going forwards.

Essentially, the original landlords have transferred their interest in the Property to the Buyer who is named in the Letter. Therefore, all payments due under the lease from {color:#bf2600}+12 September 2023 should now go to the Buyer+{color}. 

 *_Bolt action points:_* 

i)              There is +no+ requirement to acknowledge safe receipt of the Letter. But nor does it prejudice Bolt’s position if you were to do so; 

ii)             If the Buyer has not been in touch already [~accountid:60a3cea22614ec0068bec5a2] can you kindly forward a copy of the Letter to the Buyer (at the address given in the Letter) and also request the Buyer’s bank details as well as a rent demand notice for future rent payments. The next rent payment date is today (*29 September 2023*) so I suspect the Buyer will have / will shortly send through a rent demand to Bolt for the September quarter;

iii)           Given the change in ownership, Bolt should cancel any existing reoccurring payments (standing orders, direct debits etc.) benefitting the Original Landlords or their managing agents.

iv)           The Original Landlords are likely contractually obliged to pay any rent receipts after completion of the sale to the Buyer. So _if_ Bolt does make a payment to the Original Landlords before cancelling any existing arrangements, {color:#bf2600}+*then it should not pay twice!*+ {color}The Buyer should instead be provided with proof of the payment to the Original Landlords. The Buyer can then liaise with the Original Landlords (as its Sellers) to account for the payment.

v)            Please note the Letter does +not+ change Bolt’s obligation to pay any rent or other monies under the Underlease that were due to the Original Landlords before 12 September 2023 (e.g. any rent arrears or service charge arrears). Bolt should continue to make any such payments to the Original Landlords.

Please note, the Original Landlords may also write to request Bolt release them from the landlord covenants of the Underlease, if Bolt receives a letter of this nature please raise a ticket and flag it with us and we can seek further advice. 

In short, there is no automatic release for the Original Landlords from their liability, so they will have to follow the statutory procedure set down in section 8 of the Landlord and Tenant (Covenants) Act 1995. This requires the Original Landlords to apply to Bolt within 4 weeks of completion of the sale, i.e. by 10 October 2023.

{noformat}with gmv as (
select 
asc2.country_code as country,
asc2.id as city_id,
cot.driver_company_id as company_id,
cot.driver_id as driver_id,
cot.price_currency as currency,
DATE(date_add('hour', timezone_hour(at_timezone(cot.price_review_finished_timestamp, asc2.timezone)), cot.price_review_finished_timestamp)) as date,
sum(cot.ride_price) as total_ride_price,
count(*) as total_rides
from ng_public.company_order co
left join ng_public.company_order_try cot on co.id = cot.order_id and co.city_id = cot.city_id and cot.retry_to_try is null
left join ng_public.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.id = co.city_id 
where asc2.country_code = 'es'
and DATE(date_add('hour', timezone_hour(at_timezone(cot.price_review_finished_timestamp, asc2.timezone)), cot.price_review_finished_timestamp)) >= DATE('2022-01-01')
and DATE(date_add('hour', timezone_hour(at_timezone(cot.price_review_finished_timestamp, asc2.timezone)), cot.price_review_finished_timestamp)) < DATE('2023-01-01')
and cot.state in ('finished', 'client_cancelled', 'client_did_not_show') 
group by 1,2,3,4,5,6
), 
strategy as (
select gmv.*,
ifc.invoicing_strategy
from gmv 
left join ng_public.invoicing_fee_calculator ifc on ifc.company_id = gmv.company_id and ifc.start_date <= DATE(gmv.date) and coalesce(ifc.end_date,date '9999-01-01') > DATE(gmv.date) and ifc.is_active = True
where ifc.invoicing_strategy in ('driver', 'company')
), summary as (
select 
s.country,
s.currency,
date_trunc('year', s.date) as year,
case when s.invoicing_strategy = 'driver' then 'private_driver' else 'fleet' end as type,
case when s.invoicing_strategy = 'driver' then s.driver_id else s.company_id end as entity_id,
sum(total_ride_price) as total_ride_price,
sum(total_rides) as total_finished_rides
from strategy s
group by 1,2,3,4,5
)
select s.*,
coalesce(fd.invoice_issuer_name, fc.company_name) as entity_name,
coalesce(fd.invoice_issuer_vat_code, fc.vat_code) as tin_number
from summary s 
left join ng_public.fleet_driver fd on fd.id = s.entity_id and s.type = 'private_driver'
left join ng_public.fleet_company fc on fc.id = s.entity_id and s.type = 'fleet'
where s.total_ride_price < 85000
{noformat}

Simply put the 2% withholding tax should be deducted by Auchan RO from the payments it makes to Bolt Ops (EE). The agency fee invoice issued by Bolt Ops should reflect 100% of the fee and Auchan RO pays 98%.

However, considering that Bolt Ops should collect payment, deduct agency fee and transfer the payout to Auchan RO, the latter does not make payments to be withheld. Therefore, when Bolt Ops makes the payout to Auchan RO it needs to include the 2% so that Auchan can deliver it to the Romanian tax authorities.

Example:

Hello [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] ,

Below you can find my comments to the LIA. If you need any help, please let me know.

----

Question: “_Is the processing necessary to meet one or more specific objectives of any third party?_”

Original answer: “No”

Comment from the DPO: In this case, isn't the data being used to benefit the partner companies (credit card service providers)? The comment/question is made considering that the agreement between Bolt and these companies will benefit them in some way based on the credit card number.

----

Comment from the DPO: Questions “_What are the interests pursued by the company?_” and “_Describe clearly and precisely what are the interest(s) pursued._” have the same answer. Please do not copy and paste the same answer in different questions.

----

Comment from the DPO: Questions “_Describe how such interest(s) benefit(s) the individuals._” and “_Please justify the answer you gave in the previous question._” (referring to the question “_What kind of impact does this data processing activity have on the individual?_”) have the same answer. Please do not copy and paste the same answer in different questions.

----

Question “_Describe the impacts in case the processing could not take place (including any possible prejudice for the individuals in the first place, and for Bolt)._”

Comment from the DPO: The answer focuses only on impacts to the company. Are there any impacts to data subjects? If there are, please update the LIA accordingly; if there aren't, please explain why not.

----

Comment from the DPO: Questions “_Please explain why the purpose cannot be achieved without processing less personal data (or what are your doubts)._” and “_Explain why there are no less intrusive way(s) to process personal data (or what are your doubts)._” have the same answer. Please do not copy and paste the same answer in different questions.

----

Question: “_Indicate the data retention period for this data processing activity._”

Original answer: “_Until eater's account is active._”

Comment from the DPO: Please specify the reason we need to store the applied discount while the user account is active. The question arises because in the question “_Justify why all personal data collected are necessary to the purposes at stake._” it was stated that the personal data “applied discount” is stored for the following reason: “_Storing the applied discounts is necessary to maintain a record of the discounts applied to orders and assist with customer inquiries or disputes regarding applied discounts._” Therefore, once the deadline for any inquiries to be made by the user has passed, there is no longer any reason to keep the data stored, and it should be deleted or effectively anonymized.

----

Questions “_Would the individuals reasonably expect their personal data to be used for the intended purposes?_” (with original answer “Yes”) and “_Please explain in detail the reasons supporting your answer to the previous question._”, with answer “_Nature of the Service: If Bolt explicitly mentions in its terms of service, privacy policy, or during the order process that personal data may be used for calculating and applying discounts, individuals would reasonably expect such data usage._” The answer continues: “Common Industry Practice: Many e-commerce and service apps employ similar practices of analyzing payment data for discounts, and this has become a common industry practice. Individuals are likely familiar with this practice and may expect it.”

*Comment from the DPO*: First, the argument only applies to users who register once the project is up and running. In other words, future users will know that their payment data will be used to carry out this discount processing activity. However, for “old” users (i.e., users whose data was collected before the start of this new processing activity) the argument is not valid, since users expect that their credit card data will only be used to pay for the products and/or services purchased – since they had no prior information about this purpose. Hence, the importance of transparency towards users before the project is put into practice. Second, the indication that certain activities are “common practice” does not necessarily mean that they are correct and/or automatically applicable to Bolt's situation.

There are 13 issues (14 related processes), which will be solved with AI automation:

*  :green_circle: *Refund, payment, verification, safety issues, and lost phone:* in these 7 situations AI will escalate the case to CS - no matching needs to be done here. 
*  :green_circle: *Account deletion:* AI will run all checks to make sure that the user is eligible for account deletion and only then will delete the account. Actions match our process.

Bolt Drive T&Cs do cover pre authorisations: 
“7.3. After You have reserved a Motor Vehicle, we automatically pre-authorise an amount from Your Elected Payment Method to confirm the availability of the payment.“
and 
“7.9. If Bolt is unable to pre-authorise an amount from Your Elected Payment Method as indicated in Section 7.3 or debit the Service Fee from Your Elected Payment Method as indicated in Section 7.2, then Bolt is entitled to suspend or terminate the Period of Use.“
 
Moreover, note that as per Card Scheme Rules pre authorisation amounts/limits can vary depending on the policies of the card issuer (such as a bank or credit card company), the type of card (credit or debit), the card holder own limits and the merchant's policies. There is no standard or universal maximum amount that applies to all transactions. There could also be limitations from our PSP perspective, however, as I understand, the PS agreements we currently have do not cover this.
