I can see your point of view, but if the rider were to contact the bank first, their process (of the bank) usually requires the user to send them proof of the refund. Which again leads them to us.

The [KB process|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013681300] for these cases also dictates that, first, an internal investigation should be conducted to see if the refund was completed from our side. Only after we have seen that the refund was completed do we forward them to their bank. The FAQ change would then blame the bank and, to a degree, go against the KB article. 

This would again lead to the rider having a prolonged experience, which would lead to further frustration when they contact us.

Even if the information you requested were added, the rider would still need to contact us after 14 days have passed, regardless if the bank was mentioned or not.

Seeing as the CS agents should, by default, reply with information regarding the bank (if everything is ok from our side), and I believe the requested change could add more friction from the riders side, we see no current need to update the mentioned article.

I appreciate you taking the time to contact us regarding this!

Hey [~accountid:626016f5efc8a5006a559906],

The signed contract, as all our contracts, include data processing terms in Clause 4 which state that we are separate data controllers of the data processed  under the Agreement.

In relation to a controller to controller relationship, GPPR does not require the parties to enter into a Data Processing or Data Sharing Agreement. Each party acts as a separate data controller with its own responsibility to comply with GDPR and any other applicable data protection laws.

From the moment they share their data with us, the data of their employees and Admins, when they sign up to the Business Bolt account, we become a separate data controller, processing such data for our own purposes in order to provide the services to the client.

Therefore, the standard Data Processing Agreements between a Controller and a Processor according to article 28 of GDPR that they propose will not stand in our case as we are separate data controllers, and not their processors.

I will also attach a Data Sharing Agreement in case they insist to sign more data protection terms. Otherwise, we are good with the contract as is.

Thank you!

Melina

Hi [~accountid:5d53a63ba1f3290c16e637d6] 

Deb and I spoke about this in the office to get an understanding of what you are trying to achieve here. 

For your logic below, you can do this provided the Driver and the Passenger agree to any significant reductions in pricing on a trip in the App (we shouldn’t be doing this for them or taking the burden of a refund). This is because the Driver accepts a trip on the basis it will be an estimated X amount and the Passenger agrees to pay that estimated X amount and that is how the contract is formed. 

Our TnCs generally accommodate changes if the fare is higher from the original estimate (such as due to traffic conditions), but not lower, like what you’ve outlined below. This is unless there is a change in fare destination or the ride has been cancelled - however - this still requires an action on behalf of the passenger to actively change their destination in the App and for the Driver to accept this as a revision on the agreement. 

Simply because a passenger changes their mind to get out earlier, does not give them an automatic right to a refund and we shouldn’t be refunding passenger for this unless they change their end destination in the App.  An example to understand this would be like a passenger buying a train ticket from destination A to B, just because they decide to jump off at an earlier station doesn’t given them a right to a reduced ticket price - they knew what they were purchasing at the time and agreed to this. 

In short: Drivers still need to be paid the amount they were expecting and the passenger is obligated to pay it, Bolt’s App simply assists them to do this. 

Clarissa

*Rider Reports an Overcharge - UK Changes (Please see the article where changes will be applied to* [*HERE*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360012406780]*)*

*The driver didn't finish the trip on time*

*UK:* Similarly to the above, the driver can fraudulently end the trip at an incorrect destination or extend the order time to increase the final price.

*Important Note:* It is crucial that we only issue education or suspensions in cases where we are absolutely confident the fault lies with the driver, and the issue couldn't have been caused by roadblocks or similar obstacles. Always pay attention to the order criteria in Admin and check if one of the scenarios below is applicable:

# The driver ends the trip considerably further than the requested destination.
# The driver goes away from the desired destination, adds mileage, and then returns to the desired destination.
# The driver ends the trip slightly away from the desired drop-off to cross an Airport polygon twice.

If one of the scenarios is applicable, proceed with *Step 5* and *Step 6*.

*Step 5: Log the report*

* Select the correct order from the Bolt Admin Panel if not already added. The report about the driver's behavior is now collected automatically.

*Step 6: Action the Report*

*Driver Went to an Incorrect Destination or Did Not Request a Price Review*

*UK:* Leave a comment on the driver’s profile.

Decide on the next steps depending on the driver’s history:

* *First instance:* Send an outgoing ticket to the driver and educate them that intentional overcharging is unacceptable.
* *Second instance:* Warn of potential future suspension.
* *For three or more instances*: Initiate manual blocks that increase in duration. Begin with a 24-hour period, then extend to 3 days, and finally 7 days. Keep in mind that the maximum blocking period should not exceed 7 days.

h2. DSAT and ticket analysis

* In August process DSAT was 41%, data is based on 22 tickets (21 tickets from DE, one from EE). I reviewed all 22 tickets and the insights are below.
* The automation isn’t helpful in any way because it just escalates the case to the agent, whereas it could ask the user to already provide the details (e.g. receipt, bank account details).
* Agents don’t follow the KB process:
** They don’t ask about the reason for why the user paid for fuel themself, they just request compensation straight away.
** In DE there’s a market-specific process which instructs CS to try to do refund to BB (this process was introduced because Ops had many compensation requests and wanted CS to deflect some of them by offering BB refunds), but agents don’t follow it, they request compensation from Ops.
* Users get back to us asking about why it’s taking so long to get a refund - does it really take 14 days usually?
* In a few cases it looked like the original compensation request wasn’t made or actioned.
* *Root causes of the issue:*
** 41% fuel card didn’t work
** 27% unknown reason
** 10% wrong PIN of the fuel card
** 10% fuel card limit reached
** 10% wrong gas station
** 5% missing fuel card
* When the issue is that the fuel card didn’t work or the PIN was wrong, CS is supposed to escalate these issues but looks like those issues don’t get escalated because the processes for them are not a part of this particular scenario.
* Eliise said that issues with fuel cards are very common in DE, I’ll check if some fixes are planned.
* *It seems that the main reason for high AHT could be users coming back and asking when they’ll receive a refund/complaining they haven’t received the refund.*

Hi @Debora Raudberg Thank you for your questions.

* With reference to the tax treatment of the payments for the use of trademarks in Romania, I refer to article 13/3 of the double tax treaty between Estonia and Romania: “_The term “royalties” as used in this Article means payments of any kind received as a consideration for the use of, or the right to use, (…) any patent,_ +_trade mark_+_, design or model, plan, secret formula or process, or for the use of, or the right to use, any industrial, commercial or scientific equipment, or for information concerning industrial, commercial or scientific experience_.
* In what regards the difference between the trademark and other IP rights for example in Bolt Food, correct me if I am wrong, but when Bolt Ops grants a “license” for Partners to use the Bolt Food Platform (cl. 9.1 general T&Cs), Bolt Ops is allowing Partners to access the platform where they may sell their goods or services, and through which Bolt Ops performs its agency / intermediation services. I do not see a direct use of IP by Partners here. In other words, Bolt Ops is making available the final product (the platform and model which was built and is based on different IP rights) and supplying services. The IP licensing agreement and royalty payments happen between Bolt Technology (who developed the IP rights) and Bolt Ops who pays to use those rights makes the platform available to end users. In this context, from a tax perspective the payment for the access and use of the platform should be services income and not royalty income.
* In the general T&Cs the Agency Fee is exclusive for agency / intermediation services: “_In consideration for Bolt’s services as the agent for mediation of the Sales Agreements the Partner shall pay the Agency Fee to Bolt per every Order of the Client made through the Bolt Food Platform_”. Only in the specific T&Cs the Agency Fee is linked to the Bolt Market trademark.
* I also note that in clause 9.2. of the general T&Cs the Partner grants a royalty free license to Bolt for displaying on the platform, partner landing page and marketing and advertising the Partner’s trademark and all photos of the goods that are provided to Bolt. The situation here is reverse and the royalty income nature is acknowledged, so the when Bolt allows the Partner to use Bolt Market trademark it should be consistent.
* Regarding changing the wording of the agreement, if we did so for separating agency fee and royalty fee, we would have to allocate a % to each and I do not think that is something that can be easily done. It also seems that the use of trademark component would be a very reduced % as opposed to the other fees which consist in the majority of the services that are rendered. Ultimately, we do not want to complicate things and start charging royalties. Accordingly, in line with what is included in clause 9.2, what I propose is to remove the Bolt Market Trademark reference in clause 8.1 (fees and costs) of the specific terms (which considering that income is calculated over gross products price, should have no implications at all in the income received by Bolt) and amend clause 3.1. (use of Bolt Market Concept and Bolt Market Trademark) in order to make it _“_+_royalty-free_+_” non-exclusive right to use the Bolt Market Concept and the Bolt Market Trademark in Schedule 1(…)_.

The legal team is of the opinion that there is no reason to report the rider’s behaviour to the police because Bolt acts as an intermediary and any police reports shall be made by drivers if they feel doing so. Bolt has no ground to make a report. I would suggest doing the following:

# Gather information on whether there is a proven record of drivers working at the service of TVDE operators refusing service to riders with special assistance dogs. If there is a record of such refusals we need to send a reminder to the fleets (i.e the TVDE operators) saying that according to Article 8 (3) of the TVDE law (Lei n.^o^ 45/2018) pet animals shall not be refused transportation, provided they are properly accompanied and unless there is a reasonable reason, namely danger, state of health or hygiene. According to Article 14 (2) of the TVDE law (Lei n.o 45/2018), Bolt, as the electronic platform, shall ensure that persons operating on the platform comply with the law and therefore we need to take some actions.
# Assess whether there are any grounds for blocking the rider according to our T&Cs. Bolt has the right to block the rider if the rider breaches the Acceptable Use Rules, T&Cs or if it is necessary to protect the integrity of Bolt or Drivers, in particular in the event of crime.

In this case it would appear the rider is in breach of the acceptable use rules set out in section 12 of the [Terms and Conditions for Passengers|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/2z1LDv5HQEtZ4kjquemxjD/82313332068d99f196212e9245b7c650/Terms_and_Conditions_for_Passengers__valid_as_of_01.05.2023_.docx.pdf], in particular, 12.2 (d) and (l). According to the Terms and Conditions for Passengers, failing to comply with these rules enable Bolt to take any of the following actions: (a) issue a warning addressed to the Passenger or (b) immediate, temporary or permanent blocking. 

Unless drivers (or other third parties) will successfully report the rider to the police and the rider receives a criminal charge for an offence - Bolt cannot really assume that a crime was committed by the rider.

# Since this is a sensitive case we need to be careful with our approach towards the rider. We may need to approach the rider to deescalate the situation, explain that we are taking steps to remind TVDE operators that special assistance dogs should be admitted and issuing a warning to the passenger first, instead of directly enabling a hard block.

*Blog Post on Our Website* - no risks identified. It’s untargeted communication, so we do not need consent from users. 

*Telegram Announcement* - according to the Law on Information Society Services (2017) of Latvia that incorporated the ePrivacy Directive, any direct marketing should be accompanied by the consent. 

In our case, as this is the partner’s offer and a real promotion of the partner’s services, targeted to a specific group - couriers, it’s most likely a direct marketing. To place this offer in TG channel, we have to receive an opt-in from each member of the group. It’s quite unreasonable to do, and if someone from the group says “No”, we cannot deliver this message to this person, so in a group as well.

*Email Communication:* our general comms relates to the onboarding and other relevant info that is not direct marketing. Adding this promo from the partner to the emails to couriers will be qualified as the direct marketing, so *we need to have a consent from the couriers to receive any promos from our partners via email.*


*To sum up:*
It seems that 1 of 3 ways to deliver this offer is with no pain. The rest requires us to implement and get consent, that is not the desirable solution.

*What I can recommend:*
1. Create a consent form (in Google Forms, as an option, or implementing in Formaloo forms (most recommended approach)) that we can send to couriers during the sing-up process or, for existing ones, during their services, asking for the consent to receive marketing promos from Bolt related to services or products of our partners and list the categories of such partners (tax systems, discount partners, etc) and specify channels for these comms (telegram, emails, phone, etc.)
2. After that, we can send offers from these specific partners to the couriers who agreed. 
3. It will not help with the TG group messages, as if one of them disagrees, you cannot send it to the channel, until all agree to receive this.
4. This consent will at least cover some cases when we can send emails to a specific courier re promos of our partners.

{code:sql}with acceptions as (
	select 
		log.entity_type 
		, log.entity_id 
		, log.id 
		, log.created 
		, item."key" 
		, item.value 
	from ng_public.audit_log_audit_log as log
	left join ng_pii.audit_log_log_item as item 
		on item.log_id = log.id 
	where 1=1
		and log.entity_type = 'driver_registration'
		and log.created_date between date('2023-03-01') and date('2023-09-03')
		and item."key" = 'status'
		and item.value = 'accepted'
),
base as (
select 
	a.id as case_id
	, a.created
	, a.user_persona
	, a."source" 
	, b.email_address 
	, c.id as registration_id
	, case when c.status = 'accepted' then 'accepted' else 'other status' end as registration_status
	, c.created as registration_created
	, d.created
	, d.id as log_id
	, d."key"
	, d.value
from ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case as a
left join ng_pii.support_email_user_email_user as b	
	on a.user_id = b.id 
left join ng_public.fleet_driver_registration_log  as c
	on lower(b.email_address) = lower(c.email)
	and c.created <= a.created
	and c.created >= date('2023-01-01')
left join acceptions as d
	on d.entity_id = c.id
	and d.created >= a.created
where 1=1
	and a.user_persona = 'driver_lead'
	and a.created_date >= date('2023-03-01')
	and a.created_date < date('2023-09-01')
	and a."source" = 'email'
	and a.state <> 'draft'
),
base_2 as (
select 
	*
	, row_number () over (partition by case_id order by registration_created desc) as rw_nr
from base 
),
base_3 as (
select 
	registration_id
	, case_id
	, case when registration_id is not null then 'yes' else 'no' end as is_registration_found
	, registration_status
	, case when registration_status = 'accepted' and log_id is not null then 'yes' else 'no' end as is_accepted_after_case_created
	, row_number () over (partition by registration_id order by log_id desc) as rw_nr_2
from base_2 
where 1=1
	and rw_nr = 1
)
select 
	registration_status
	, is_accepted_after_case_created
	, count(registration_id) as registrations_count
from base_3
where 1=1
	and rw_nr_2 = 1
	and is_registration_found = 'yes'
group by 1, 2{code}

{code:sql}WITH marking_time AS (
SELECT 
a.created AS marking_time,
a.order_id,
a.city_id,
a.comment
FROM ng_public.fraud_action_order_action a
WHERE a.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND a.comment LIKE 'By profiling%'
AND a."action" = 'mark_order_as_fraud'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
),
deducting_time AS (
SELECT 
a.created AS deducting_time,
a.order_id,
a.city_id,
a.comment
FROM ng_public.fraud_action_order_action a
WHERE a.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND a.comment LIKE 'By profiling%'
AND a."action" IN ('deduct_cash_campaign_bonus','refund_balance_order_from_driver')
AND a.status = 'success'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
SELECT 
MONTH(mt.marking_time) AS month,
--'https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/' || CAST(a.order_id AS varchar) || '/' || CAST(a.city_id AS varchar) AS orderlink,
--DATE_DIFF('hour',mt.marking_time,dt.deducting_time) AS action_delayed_hours
CASE WHEN DATE_DIFF('hour',mt.marking_time,dt.deducting_time) > 0 THEN 'multiple_hours' ELSE 'not_delayed' END AS time_to_deduct_after_marking_in_hours,
APPROX_DISTINCT(a.order_id,0.0041) AS count_orders
FROM ng_public.fraud_action_order_action a
JOIN marking_time mt ON a.order_id = mt.order_id AND a.city_id = mt.city_id 
JOIN deducting_time dt ON a.order_id = dt.order_id AND a.city_id = dt.city_id
WHERE a.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND mt.comment = dt.comment
GROUP BY 1,2
ORDER BY 1 DESC {code}

Title: Recall a Strong Leader in Your Life

Hello [~accountid:601d5136b7bda90068fd6d6c],

The new refund action in Beehive represents modified interaction “_Does it solve your issue? Yes/No”_. Refund happens only when the user accepts it (“_Yes, issue is solved”_). If no action is taken by the user, interaction will expire and the ticket will get closed. 

To illustrate, imagine a scenario where a user has a non-refund related inquiry. When the question “_Does it solve your issue?_” is sent, if the user doesn’t select _“Yes/No”,_ the system closes the inquiry. But if the user comes back later and creates a new ticket, CS will assist them again, continuing the support process and taking all necessary actions.

This same principle applies to refunds. If the user doesn't accept/decline the refund within the 48hrs, and the request is closed, but they return to inform us that the problem persists - CS will continue to address the issue, including giving a refund and all other required actions.

It's crucial to note that the process has an action: *“Inform the rider that they need to accept or decline the refund, otherwise it will expire”*. Clear communication at this stage is key to efficiently resolving cases and preventing repetitive inquiries.

Hi



We have discussed internally with the privacy team, and overall, we may suggest the following 2 approaches:



1] One is briefly described by the section "*Manual collected opt-ins before communicating a specific offer" -* [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/2587067086/Third-Party+Offers|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/2587067086/Third-Party+Offers|smart-link] .

Basically, we need to ask users explicit consent to receive our partner related comms. Also, this is the case where we *can mention the details of the partner* that wants to send out the offer - and our suggestion is that we indicate the specific partner.

Preferably, we suggest to try get the consent via email. *Please note that in this case we will only receive consent to share offers of this specific partner.*



2] However, there is a bigger question of getting consents for *third party* *marketing generally*. Having a look at the issue in more detail, we understand that the "Partner Offers" feature was a compromise between marketing and privacy, *and factually  its not very lawful under the GDPR*.

Ideally, we want all users (including drivers, Bolt Food, etc) to give their *explicit consents* for *partner offers*:

2.1] This can be done via toggles, as suggested in this page - [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/2587067086/Third-Party+Offers|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/2587067086/Third-Party+Offers|smart-link]  (under "Marketing Channels") - so: 1. users have a separate consent toggle 2. toggle for partner offers should be *off by default*, and we may only suggest the user to turn it on when we ask for explicit consent.

2.2] As the toggle feature is not readily available, other mediums for obtaining explicit consent for partner marketing can be used - such as email. As we understand, we do not have lawfully collected consents at all right now, because:

* only the Rider App has a separate consent toggle for users (not drivers) and still, its on by default (*which is unlawful in the EU)*, and
* in other cases, there is no option for a separate consent for partner marketing at all.

If we are interested in lawfully sending out the marketing comms of third parties *generally* (encompassing the case of this particular ticket), we suggest considering a campaign where we obtain explicit consents for *partner marketing*.

Then, in principal, we could also send out partner marketing mentioning a particular offer through other regular channels (email, push notifications, app-inboxes, in-app messages, SMS), not only the Partner Offers feature [~accountid:5cf539ddc756c10f35f28d01].



*Please confirm if our understanding provided above is correct* [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35]*.* If yes:

* act in accordance to p.1 and deal with the more general problem later under p.2; or
* try to get consents as described by p 2.2 (so, via email or other medium) or 2.1. - but we understand that implementing toggles is not possible to do asap.

When you decide to proceed with options 2.1 or 2.2 - let us know, and we will further discuss the details how this can be done.
